geometry.locator: Nominatim search result for a rest area on the Haizi Mountain route, Daocheng County

method: Reuses the already-sourced approximate campus point for site:lhaaso-haizi-mountain (OpenStreetMap/Nominatim geocode of a rest area on the Haizi Mountain route, precision_m 5000) verbatim; no new coordinate is derived. A tighter value (29d21'27.6"N, 100d08'19.6"E) is repeatedly attributed to the LHAASO Science Book (arXiv:1905.02773) by independent web-search text extracts, but every attempt this session to fetch that PDF/HTML directly (WebFetch, ar5iv, arxiv.org/html, and an r.jina.ai text-extraction proxy) returned only binary/garbled content or a 404 -- the value could not be seen verbatim in a fetched page this session and is NOT used here (see worklog candidate-correction list, flagged unverified). KM2A is independently sourced as circular (radius ~575 m core, ~635 m outer guard ring) and WCDA as 78,000 m2 (two 150x150 m pools + one 300x110 m pool), but neither can be drawn: both would need to be centred on a coordinate precise to well under the shapes' own size, and the only coordinate available this session (precision_m 5000) is far too coarse (geometry-derived-from-coarse-anchor) -- see worklog backlog.
name: LHAASO (reference point)
notes: KM2A (circular, ~575-635 m radius) and WCDA (78,000 m2, two 150x150 m pools plus one 300x110 m pool) are described with enough shape/size detail to draw, but not with a coordinate precise enough to anchor them honestly this session; see method and worklog backlog.

QA pass (2026-09-21): added the ODbL-1.0 licence this record omitted despite its own `method`/`geometry.note` stating the coordinate is a verbatim Nominatim (OpenStreetMap) geocode; the underlying `src:cosmic-gamma-nominatim-haizi-mountain` source predates the A25 `openstreetmap` source_type convention (it is typed `geocoder`) and its Nominatim response did not record a specific osm_id, so `osm.elements` is left null rather than invented. No coordinate or claim changed.

summary.plain: The high-altitude LHAASO cosmic-ray and gamma-ray observatory on Haizi Mountain, Sichuan, shown here as a single approximate reference point.
